title: Spelling and Misspelt Words: Writing the Word Right

questions.question: Which word is spelled INCORRECTLY?
questions.rationale: Correct: religion. The others obey the i-before-e rule — believe (i before e), receive (ei after c) — while weird is a memorised exception ('we are weird').

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelled word:
questions.rationale: Accommodate takes two c's and two m's — the most misspelt word in English. Remember: accommodation has room for two of everything.

questions.question: The correct spelling of the word meaning 'to go before' is:
questions.rationale: Only exceed, proceed, and succeed take -ceed; supersede alone takes -sede; every other word in the family takes -cede — precede, concede, recede, secede.

questions.question: Which sentence contains a spelling error?
questions.rationale: Correct: necessary — one c, two s's ('one collar and two sleeves'). The other three are the correct forms of committee, definite, and separately.

questions.question: The plural of 'knife' and 'leaf' respectively is:
questions.rationale: Most -f/-fe nouns change to -ves (knife-knives, leaf-leaves, wolf-wolves), but a few keep plain -s: roofs, chiefs, beliefs, cliffs.

questions.question: Which is the correct British spelling, as used in Indian exams?
questions.rationale: British/Indian convention: -our (colour), -re (centre), -ise (organise), doubled l in travelled — the American flips (color, center, organize) stay consistent only within US texts.

questions.question: Which word has a silent 'b'?
questions.rationale: Debt (and doubt, subtle, dumb) keep a silent b from Latin debitum. Island has a silent s, psychology a silent p, and Wednesday a silent first d.

questions.question: The correct spelling is:
questions.rationale: Millennium carries double l AND double n. Anniversary-style mnemonic: a millennium is a thousand years — too long to spell with single letters.

questions.question: 'Begin' becomes 'beginning' with doubled n because:
options: All -ing forms double the final consonant
The word ends in a vowel
The final syllable is stressed (be-GIN), so the single final consonant doubles
It is an exception to every rule
questions.rationale: Doubling applies when a two-syllable word is stressed on the final syllable (begin, refer, permit), but not when stress falls earlier — hence visiting, benefited, developed stay single.

questions.question: Spot the correctly spelled word:
questions.rationale: Privilege (no d between e and g) is correct. The rogues' gallery catches the rest: separate (a-r-a), definitely (no a), government (includes the n).
